summary: Install-time dropper: binding.gyp executes obfuscated AES-encrypted payload via node-gyp
details: Package ships a binding.gyp with no native C/C++ sources (sources list only a fake stub, type:none) whose sole purpose is to trigger node-gyp at npm install and run `node index.js` via GYP command-expansion (`<!(env node index.js...)`). index.js is a Caesar-shift-3-encoded eval wrapper that, once decoded, uses createDecipheriv("aes-128-gcm",...) with hardcoded hex key/iv/aad to decrypt an inline string (eval'd) and to decrypt + gunzip the bundled `data.bin`, then spawns a Bun or Node child process and pipes the decrypted payload into it as stdin for execution. The multi-layer obfuscation (Caesar + AES-128-GCM + gzip) hides the real payload from static inspection, and the whole chain fires automatically on `npm install` with no user action. The package name has no legitimate relationship to native-addon building, and no genuine addon code is present — the binding.gyp is purely a lifecycle vector.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
